tokens.TITLE: Shane Boyer: New York in Every Frame
tokens.META_DESCRIPTION: Shane Boyer (@shaneboyerr) is the POV filmmaker behind TikTok's most cinematic New York — 2.5M+ followers and 11.7M-view brand films for Polaroid & YSL.
tokens.KEYWORDS: Shane Boyer, shaneboyerr, POV filmmaker, New York creator, TikTok, skateboarding, Polaroid, YSL, Canada Goose, DJI, Meta Ray-Bans, content creator, influencer marketing
tokens.HEADLINE_GOLD: films New York like nowhere else.
tokens.DEK: The POV filmmaker behind some of TikTok's most-shared New York footage — 2.5M followers, 11.7M-view brand films, and a rooftop-to-subway eye that Polaroid, YSL and Canada Goose keep booking.
tokens.HERO_CAPTION: Shane Boyer on a Manhattan ledge — a 4M-view TikTok. Courtesy @shaneboyerr.
tokens.STAT_FOOTNOTE: TikTok figures verified July 2026; Instagram (200K+) per DGTL. Top-video views are from Shane's own TikTok posts.
tokens.LEAD: Shane Boyer makes you feel like you're standing on the ledge with him. For five years he has pointed a camera at New York — from Central Park rooftops to rain-slick subway platforms — and turned a skater's eye for the city into an audience of 2.5 million people who show up for every frame.
tokens.BODY_1: It's a specific kind of talent: not just being somewhere striking, but framing it so the feeling travels. Boyer's POV videos read like short films — colour-graded, patient, scored — and they move the way the best short-form does, on the strength of the shot rather than a trend. That's the asset a brand can't fake, and the reason his numbers keep compounding.
tokens.H2_1: A city everyone has filmed, shot like no one else
tokens.BODY_2: New York is the most-filmed city on earth, which is exactly why Boyer stands out in it. He finds the angle nobody else climbs to — the ledge, the empty theatre, the platform as the train blurs past — and holds it long enough to feel like a memory. His audience doesn't watch for information; they watch for the mood. That's a rare, durable kind of attention.
tokens.PULLQUOTE: A city everyone has filmed — shot like no one else has.
tokens.PULLQUOTE_CITE: — The DGTL Influence view on Shane Boyer
tokens.BODY_3: Because his taste sells the product for him. His Polaroid Go film — a quiet POV on a set of train tracks — passed 11.7 million views because it looked like Shane, not like an ad. That's the whole thesis of creator-led work: hand the brief to someone an audience already trusts, and the recommendation reads as continuity. Boyer's brand partners have included Polaroid, YSL, Canada Goose, DJI and Meta Ray-Bans — each folded into his world rather than bolted onto it.
tokens.CALLOUT_1: POV that reads as authentic — the recommendation feels like the creator, not the campaign.
tokens.CALLOUT_2: A signature look: cinematic New York, colour-graded and patient.
tokens.CALLOUT_3: An audience that shows up for the mood, not just the moment.
tokens.CALLOUT_4: One creator delivering cinema-grade short-form, on schedule.
tokens.BODY_4: It's why a brand chasing a feeling — arrival, escape, the shot you wish you'd taken — is often better served by one Shane Boyer than a stack of generic placements. The reach is the headline; the taste is the reason it works.
tokens.STATCALLOUT_CAP: One brand film, 11.7M views. Boyer's Polaroid Go POV out-travelled campaigns with many times the budget — because it looked like his own work, not an advert.
